critical_code_review_comments: programNav.js: section/hub/program lookup maps are built deterministically and idempotently. The `if (p.link && !PROGRAM_NAV[p.link])` guard on line 56 correctly prevents collisions when the same program slug is referenced by multiple hubs.

Breadcrumbs.jsx: returns null on routeId === 'home' or unwired routes (only home in trail → suppressed by length<2 check), which keeps the homepage and unrelated pages clean. Active item correctly renders as <span aria-current='page'> with testid suffix '-current'.
HubPeerNav.jsx: lookupProgram→peerPrograms→pathFor chain is clean; renders an 'empty' message gracefully if a hub had a single program (none currently do — confirmed 5 peers on atlas_desierto/4n_5d).

Minor (non-blocking): Breadcrumbs absolute-positions itself over the hero with top padding 88/96px. On hub pages where the hero is the first section this lays out correctly. If a future Sur page lacks a hero (full-bleed), the breadcrumb may overlay normal body text — recommend a defensive `position: relative` wrapper or a fallback static layout when the parent has no hero. No visual regression observed today.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 8 fully green for Phase 1 'Opción B' (Breadcrumbs + HubPeerNav) across the Sur de Marruecos section in ES/EN/FR. Available testids: 'breadcrumbs' on the <nav>, plus per-item children 'bc-home', 'bc-tours', 'bc-section' (or '-current' suffix when it is the last/current node), 'bc-hub' (or 'bc-hub-current'), 'bc-program-current'. HubPeerNav exposes 'hub-peer-nav', 'hub-peer-nav-back', and 'hub-peer-program-{id}' (e.g. 'hub-peer-program-ad-5-6'). Programs wired in PROGRAM_NAV are the 22+ Sur programs whose hubs are listed in SECTION_HUBS.tourSouth. Future hubs (Norte/Escapadas/Gran Sur) intentionally return null from <Breadcrumbs/> for their PROGRAM pages (only the section-level pages render breadcrumb because their section label exists in the SECTIONS map). The breadcrumb absolute-positions over the hero with a glass strip — verified visually rendered fine on every tested page.
